extractedItems.title: Playing a Ball from a Bad Lie
extractedItems.question: Your ball lands in an old footprint in a bunker, but there is no specific rule. What must you do?

choices.text: Take a free drop out of the footprint
Play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable
Move the ball to a better spot without penalty
Ask your opponent for help and re-drop without penalty

extractedItems.explanation: If a bad lie is not covered by other rules, you must play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable, with penalties as per unplayable ball rules.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl standing next to her ball in an old footprint in a bunker, looking at the lie thoughtfully.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Girl stands in bunker looking at her ball in an old footprint.

extractedItems.title: Declaring a Ball Unplayable in a Bunker
extractedItems.question: If your ball is unplayable in a bunker, how many penalty strokes does it cost to drop the ball outside the bunker?

choices.text: No penalty
1 penalty stroke
2 penalty strokes
3 penalty strokes

extractedItems.explanation: Dropping outside the bunker on the extension of the line costs 2 penalty strokes.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy preparing to drop a ball behind a bunker after declaring his ball unplayable, holding an iron.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Boy drops a golf ball behind a bunker with a club in hand.

extractedItems.title: Options for an Unplayable Ball in a Bunker
extractedItems.question: Which of these are options you have if your ball is unplayable in a bunker?

choices.text: Drop within 2 club-lengths in the bunker (1 penalty stroke)
Go back on the line in the bunker and drop (1 penalty stroke)
Replay from your last spot, even from the tee (1 penalty stroke)
Drop outside the bunker going back on the line (2 penalty strokes)
Take a free drop outside the bunker

extractedItems.explanation: All except a free drop outside the bunker are correct options, with different penalties.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl standing in a bunker weighing her options for an unplayable ball, visualising various drop choices.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Girl in bunker looking at possible places to drop her ball.

extractedItems.title: Dropping After Returning to Last Stroke Location
extractedItems.question: If you decide to return to the spot of your last stroke from a bunker and declare the ball unplayable, how far are you allowed to drop from that spot?

choices.text: Exactly on the same spot
Within 1 club-length
Within 2 club-lengths
Anywhere on the green

extractedItems.explanation: You may drop within 1 club-length from the spot of your last stroke.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy on the fairway about to drop a new ball within one club-length from where he just hit his last shot.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Boy measures and drops a new ball near his last shot location on fairway.

reviewedItems.title: Declaring a Ball Unplayable in a Bunker
reviewedItems.question: If your ball is unplayable in a bunker and you choose to drop it outside the bunker behind where it lay, how many penalty strokes must you add?

choices.text: No penalty
1 penalty stroke
2 penalty strokes
3 penalty strokes

reviewedItems.explanation: According to the rules, choosing to drop outside the bunker behind the original spot incurs a two-stroke penalty.

reviewedItems.title: Options for an Unplayable Ball in a Bunker
reviewedItems.question: If your ball is unplayable in a bunker, which of these are legal options you can choose? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Drop within 2 club-lengths in the bunker (1 penalty stroke)
Go back on the line in the bunker and drop (1 penalty stroke)
Replay from your last spot, even from the tee (1 penalty stroke)
Drop outside the bunker going back on the line (2 penalty strokes)
Take a free drop outside the bunker

reviewedItems.explanation: You may drop within the bunker using either the two club-length or back-on-the-line options, replay the shot, or drop outside the bunker with a two-stroke penalty. A free drop outside the bunker is not allowed.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl standing in a bunker thinking over her options for an unplayable ball, considering various legal drop spots within and outside the bunker.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Girl in bunker looking at possible places to drop her ball.

reviewedItems.title: Dropping After Returning to Last Stroke Location
reviewedItems.question: If you decide to return to the spot of your last shot and declare your ball unplayable, how far from that spot are you allowed to drop your ball under the rules?

choices.text: Exactly on the same spot
Within 1 club-length
Within 2 club-lengths
Anywhere on the green

reviewedItems.explanation: You must drop the ball within one club-length of where your last shot was played, not closer to the hole.
